title: MCP Ecosystem in 2026
content:
## Overview

The Model Context Protocol (MCP), released by Anthropic in November 2024, crossed from an interesting open standard to the **default integration layer for agent runtimes** during 2025–2026. As of mid-2026, every major LLM host natively speaks MCP: Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Cursor, the ChatGPT desktop app, and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway.

---

## Server Ecosystem Scale

The public MCP server count grew from a few dozen at launch (late 2024) to over **5,000 public servers** by mid-2026. Server categories include:

- **Databases:** Postgres, MySQL, SQLite, Redis, MongoDB
- **File storage:** Google Drive, Box, Dropbox, OneDrive
- **Dev tools:** GitHub, GitLab, Jira, Linear, Asana
- **Communication:** Slack, Gmail, Outlook, Discord
- **Web automation:** Brave Search, Puppeteer, Playwright, Firecrawl
- **Data/BI:** BigQuery, Snowflake, dbt, Metabase
- **Infrastructure:** AWS, GCP, Kubernetes, Terraform

Anthropic maintains a curated registry at `github.com/modelcontextprotocol/servers`. Community-maintained directories (mcp.so, glama.ai/mcp/servers) index hundreds more.

---

## MCP 2026-07-28 Specification (Release Candidate)

The largest revision of the protocol since launch. Three major changes:

### 1. Stateless HTTP Core

The transport layer is redesigned around ordinary HTTP. MCP servers no longer require persistent connections — each request is self-contained. This allows MCP servers to run on serverless infrastructure (AWS Lambda, Google Cloud Run, Cloudflare Workers) and scale horizontally without sticky sessions.

The earlier stdio (subprocess) transport remains supported for local development.

### 2. Extensions: MCP Apps and Tasks

**MCP Apps** — servers can return server-rendered UI fragments (HTML, markdown, structured card layouts) that clients render inline. This enables richer tool responses beyond raw JSON, useful for display-heavy use cases like dashboards or code diffs.

**Tasks extension** — a standardized mechanism for long-running asynchronous work. A tool call returns a task handle; the client polls or subscribes via SSE for completion. This replaces the ad-hoc polling implementations that had proliferated across the ecosystem.

### 3. OAuth/OIDC-Aligned Authorization

The auth spec now aligns with standard OAuth 2.1 and OpenID Connect flows, replacing the earlier custom token model. Enterprise deployments can integrate MCP servers directly with existing identity providers (Okta, Azure AD, Auth0) without custom adapters. A browser-based OAuth flow grants short-lived tokens — matching the security model of SaaS integrations developers already manage.

---

## Deployment Patterns

### Remote vs. Local Servers

In early MCP (2024), most servers ran locally via `stdio` transport. By 2026, the majority of production deployments use HTTP/SSE transport, running servers remotely and shared across teams. Several MCP-as-a-service providers offer hosted, pre-authenticated connectors — users connect once via OAuth and share the server endpoint across projects.

### Multi-Client Server Sharing

A single remote MCP server can now serve multiple Claude Code sessions simultaneously. This is how enterprise teams share internal data connectors — one Postgres MCP server or one internal knowledge-base MCP server is authenticated once and available to all team members.

### Agent-to-Agent Communication

Claude Code's multi-agent feature uses MCP as the communication channel when subagents run remotely. A coordinator on one container can dispatch work to subagents on separate cloud containers, with results returned via standard MCP tool responses. This architecture scales agentic pipelines without bespoke orchestration code.

---

## Claude Code Integration

Claude Code supports MCP servers defined in `.claude/settings.json`:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "github": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "@modelcontextprotocol/server-github"]
    },
    "postgres": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "@modelcontextprotocol/server-postgres", "postgresql://localhost/mydb"]
    }
  }
}
```

New in 2026: remote HTTP servers can be added by URL, eliminating the need to install local packages:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "my-internal-tool": {
      "url": "https://mcp.internal.example.com/my-tool",
      "auth": { "type": "oauth" }
    }
  }
}
```

---

## Building MCP Servers

The official SDKs cover TypeScript, Python, and (as of 2026) Go and Rust:

```python
from mcp.server import Server
from mcp.types import Tool

app = Server("my-server")

@app.tool()
async def search_docs(query: str) -> str:
    """Search internal documentation."""
    results = await internal_search(query)
    return format_results(results)
```

The stateless HTTP model (new in the 2026 spec) means a server is just an HTTP handler — no daemon process or persistent state required.
